newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka sees tea output 250-255 mln kg 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka sees tea output 250-255 mln kg 1997.

text.p: The Sri Lanka Tea Board said on Monday it expected the country's total tea production to average between 250 and 255 million kg this year.
This compares with figures from the United Nations Food & Agriculture Organisation (FAO), which estimated Sri Lankan production at 258.4 million kg last year.
Tea Board Chairman Clifford Ratwatte told Reuters Sri Lankan production was likely to rise over the next few years and could top 300 million kg a year within five years.
He said tea prices were holding firm and Sri Lanka's total net income from tea exports this year should exceed 35 billion rupees, up from 32 billion last year.
"On production, there may not be much of a variation from last year - 250, maybe 255 million kg, that's our target," Ratwatte said in an interview.
"Definitely, we will be a bigger exporter than Kenya this year because Kenya suffered a severe drought in the first three or four months of the year," he said.

According to the FAO, Sri Lankan tea exports reached 244 million kg in 1996, but the country was just overtaken by Kenya as the world's biggest exporter. Kenya made sales of some 244.2 million kg, the FAO said.
"We should top last year's (net income). If last year was 32 billion rupees, we should go over 35 billion this year if prices remain stable as they are now."

He said privatisation of Sri Lanka's tea plantations, combined with replanting and in-filling of crops, proper fertilisation and the increased use of compost would boost output steadily over the next decade.
"If all this happens...we could reach 300 million kg in another five years. But it wouldn't be in less than five years," he said.
